findings: Remark, l.496–498, statement unaffected: for « La proposition 7 … sont donc vrais aussi dans le cas affin » the Remark needs V sweepable for G regarded as a group of projective automorphisms, and it leaves this implicit. The step is immediate: the action is unchanged, so the same compact generating domain serves (IsBalayableFor.affToProj).
questions: « connexe » in the Remark's last sentence (l.503–504). The Remark's hypotheses (l.493–495) do not print « connexe ». Its conclusion « La proposition 7 et son corollaire sont donc vrais aussi dans le cas affin » refers to Prop. 7, which assumes it. The statement it announces (« on a l'énoncé : », Prop. 7′, l.507–508) prints it. Reading taken: Prop. 7's hypotheses, connectedness included (cas_affin's third conjunct is under PreconnectedSpace V; the first two need no connectedness). This also coincides with the protocol's standing convention that a « variété » is connected. Both readings give the same Lean statement. The literal alternative, with no connectedness, is false in every dimension ≥ 1 (Benzecri.not_deuxPointsDansPocheAffineSansConnexe: ℝⁿ⁺¹ minus the hyperplane x₀ = 0, sweepable for its affine automorphisms, with the pocket {0 < x₀ < 1}, cote x₀; the points ±½𝟙 lie on the two sides and no homeomorphism moves both into one side). So I consider the reading forced by the text, and marked the row; the auditor should confirm that this is not an open reading.

kb_proposals: Affine to projective automorphisms: GXAut.affToProj : GXAut (GAR n) ℝⁿ V →* GXAut (GSR n) (S n) V for projOfAff. Each automorphism acts as itself (affToProj_smul is rfl), and IsBalayableFor.affToProj keeps the compact. The general forms are IsGXMorphism.transport and GXAut.transport, for any open embedding of models that is equivariant through G' →* G. Use them wherever an affine statement is derived from its projective twin, for example T-bz-c2-theoreme-affine.

Cheap affine manifolds with automorphisms: GXAut.ofOpens builds an automorphism of an open subset U of the model from any g ∈ G with g • x ∈ U ↔ x ∈ U. On Opens of the model, chartAt X x y = y.val holds by rfl. Ready-made examples: the half-space demiEspaceOuvert n, which is homogeneous and has the pocket {0 < x₀ < 1} with cote x₀ (not constant); and the hyperplane complement complHyperplan n, which is disconnected, homogeneous and has the same pocket.

A pocket with a non-constant cote exists in every dimension ≥ 1 (exists_isPocheAff_demiEspace, by exemple_poche_affine). Use it as the non-vacuity witness for any pocket statement that must survive OQ-61 (a). In dimension 0 every affine function is constant, so no such pocket exists there.

Pitfall: on a subtype of TopologicalSpace.Opens, `rw [himg]` with himg : Subtype.val '' U = … can fail after `rw [← IsInducing.subtypeVal.isPreconnected_image]`, because the coercion differs syntactically. Use `convert h using 1; ext` instead.
notes: One new file, sorry-free, standard axioms only (#print axioms checked for all 40 declarations). lake build BenzecriScaffold.Chapter2.CasAffin rebuilt only that module. Imports: Benzecri.Chapter2.Compact, and Benzecri.Chapter2.Projection for translationAut. Both labels are MARKED. Proof: Prop. 7′ is Prop. 7 and its corollary (compact_dans_poche, deux_points_dans_poche, strict) applied to projOfAff, the image of G under GXAut.affToProj, and the pocket IsPocheAff.toPocheProj j for j : ℝⁿ ≃ᵃ H₀. That is the Remark's own argument. The marks depend on neither OQ-45 nor OQ-61: Prop. 7 holds in every dimension, and under OQ-61 (a) IsPocheAff would only gain a hypothesis. Non-vacuity, as dispatched: ℝⁿ with its translations (translationSubgroup n = closure of range translationAut) and isPocheAff_model, in every dimension. A better witness: for every n + 1 ≥ 1, the open half-space {x₀ > 0}, swept from one point by its affine automorphisms, with a NON-CONSTANT cote. It is the witness the T-bz-c2-compact REPORT asked for, and via cas_affin its projective image also witnesses Prop. 7 with a non-constant cote. The file builds strict-clean (lake env lean -DwarningAsError=true shows no warning). At graduation, check name clashes against T-bz-c2-developpement's Developpement.lean, which I did not read, as dispatched: GXAut.transport, IsGXMorphism.transport and GXAut.ofOpens are generic names that a developing-map file might also define. The strict library has none of the 40 names (grep). The roadmap evidence's line references are right: projOfAff Poches.lean:649, hasGroupoid_projOfAff :657, toPocheProj :730, isPocheAff_model :1297, GXAut.ofBijective Classes.lean:285, IsBalayableFor :303.
